subject: African lion
title: Lions Now Kill Zebras 3 Times Less Often, Because of an Ant

scenes.text: Kenya's lions are losing their hunts to an ant.
Where this tiny invader spread, lions kill zebras nearly three times less often.
It never touches a lion. It kills off the ants guarding thorn trees.
Those ants bite any elephant that eats their tree. Without them, elephants wreck trees five to seven times faster.
The bush opens up, and lions lose the cover they need to ambush.
So lions switched to buffalo: zero percent of kills in 2003, forty-two percent by 2020.

description:
At Ol Pejeta in Kenya, the invasive big-headed ant kills the native acacia ants that defend whistling-thorn trees from elephants.
In invaded areas elephants break trees five to seven times more, the bush opens up, and zebra kills by lions were 2.87 times higher in uninvaded areas (Science, 2024).
Zebras fell from 67% of lion kills in 2003 to 42% in 2020, while buffalo rose from 0% to 42%.
Did you expect an ant to change what lions eat?
first_comment: Lion numbers held steady because they took on buffalo, which are bigger and need teamwork to bring down. What tiny animal do you think has the biggest effect on its ecosystem?
